# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

I have the picture. Answers to your three questions first, then the forks I need you to settle before I start cutting.

**`maintenance`** — it's two unrelated things wearing one hat:
- `mechanism` is a finished rollout's flag. `engine/served-by.mjs:44` lists `baselining | updates | versioned`; baselining was deleted in Phase 5, `updates` is only a legacy spelling of `versioned`, and `DEFAULT_MECHANISM` is `versioned`. So every member declares the only value that exists. It's dead weight, kept alive only so a straggler declaring `baselining` is told loudly rather than served silently.
- `delivery` (`auto-merge` | `review`) is genuinely live and genuinely per-member — `engine/scheduler/land-pr.mjs:110`, `deliver-generated.mjs:131`, `update/worker.mjs:134` all branch on it. It's the one real setting in the block.

**`endpoints`** — no defence. It's an agentic-session invocation URL + the *name* of the Actions secret holding its token (`repo-context.mjs:341`), and "endpoints" says none of that. Renaming to `agenticTaskInvocationEndpoints` is right.

**`claudinite.updated` / `ref` — not redundant, but worse than redundant: stale by construction.** Only `vendoring/apply-vendor-set.mjs` (full re-vendor / bootstrap) writes them; the nightly versioned converge (`updates/engine-update.mjs:191`, `updates/pack-update.mjs:386`) stamps versions and nothing else. Yet four live readers consume them: the #328 anti-rewind guard (`apply-vendor-set.mjs:62` — prior stamped ref must be an ancestor), the update task's precondition (`tasks/update/task.mjs:41`), sheepdog drift detection (`drift-issues.mjs:73,189`), and the dashboard (`fleet.mjs:87`). That mismatch is exactly why our own `claudinite-lifecycle` RULES already say "never judge freshness by `updated` or `ref`". So deleting them is a real change with four call sites to rework, not a cleanup — and once `packVersions` moves out and they go, yes, `engineVersion` bubbles up and the block dissolves.

Three forks I can't take back:

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

- adopt-claudinite: Bootstrap Claudinite into a consuming repo — mount, hooks, checks, skills. Use when asked to bootstrap, adopt, or set up Claudinite, or to baseline a repo to pick up updates.
- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- ci-performance-evaluation: Method for finding where a repo's CI time actually goes and what is worth fixing. Use when CI feels slow, when investigating a runtime regression, or when the weekly ci-performance task hands you a finding.
- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.
- extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- generate-project-instructions: Decompose a project into its pack facets (working-style class, technology, aspect, domain) and extract its working instructions into reusable canon packs plus the project's own local packs (.claudinite/local_packs/). Use when a project has no established working style yet, or it exhibits a facet no pack covers — during bootstrap of a fresh/empty repo, or on an uplevel request.
- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- single-branch-status: Assess one branch's landed status — merged, already-in-main, superseded, orphaned, or genuine unmerged work — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single branch is safe to delete, judging by content not the ref's name (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-branches task hands you branches to assess).
- single-issue-triage: Triage one open issue and take the first applicable action — close-if-implemented, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, or leave. Use when acting on a single issue; "implemented in main" must be verified against main's current content and the default is to comment, not close (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-issues task hands you issues to triage).
- single-pr-status: Assess one open pull request's landed status — keep-open, or closeable (merged, already-in-main, superseded, stale) — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single PR should stay open, judging by its commits and diff not its title (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-prs task hands you PRs to assess).
- unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.
- verify-in-production: Decide whether a change that has merged can only be proven in production, and if so file the verification that comes back on its own once it is live. Use immediately after the merge, beside the conversation capture — never before, and not on request.
- writing-claudinite-skills: Authoring or changing a skill in the Claudinite corpus — SKILL.md conventions, where a skill's checks and tests live, catalog and pack wiring. Use when creating or editing a pack's skills/<name>/ in the canon; a consumer project's own agent docs are authoring-agent-docs' turf.
- writing-migration-plans: Where a plan and a design live, and how to order a plan's phases so nothing stalls mid-run — the plan is a tracking issue (never a plan document in the repo), the design doc carries only the end state with rationale and alternatives; front-load the out-of-band setup, write ALL the code including the cleanup and take one approval for the stack, then chain every execution step to the verification of the one before it as a queued continuation, and keep the tracking issue append-only while implementing. Use BEFORE writing any DESIGN.md, migration plan, phased implementation plan, rollout or cutover plan — including the moment you are about to create a docs/<initiative>/ file — and when working through a plan's tracking issue.
- writing-tasks: The contract a Claudinite task is written to — the declaration's fields, the code-work and agentic phases, the precondition as the only decision point, ordering, and how a work item converges. Use when writing or changing a tasks/<name>/task.mjs or its worker, or when a task-declaration check fires.
- writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.
- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one — Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
- docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation.
- import-memory: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data.
- morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx or .potx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.

input.title: Restructure the member declaration: .claudinite-settings.json, versions on pack entries, dissolve the maintenance and claudinite blocks
input.body:
The member declaration has accumulated three blocks that no longer say what they are, and one that answers a question nobody asks any more. Owner decisions, this session:

## The end state

```jsonc
{
  "engineVersion": "60820.1",
  "dailyClaudiniteUpdatesRequirePrReview": true,   // optional; absent = update PRs auto-merge
  "packs": [
    { "id": "basics", "version": "60822.1" },
    { "id": "claudinite-growth", "version": "60820.3", "config": { … } }
  ],
  "rules": { … },
  "accept": [ … ],
  "taskScheduler": { "agenticTaskInvocationEndpoints": { … }, "dailyHour": 5, … }
}
```

1. **The file is `.claudinite-settings.json`.** It has never been a file of checks.
2. **A pack's installed version lives on that pack's own entry** (`version`), not in a central `claudinite.packVersions` map keyed by a spelling that a rename can invalidate.
3. **`maintenance` goes.** `mechanism` is the record of a rollout that finished — `versioned` is the only mechanism a repo can be served by, and `baselining` names something that no longer exists. `delivery` is real but every member says `auto-merge`, so it becomes a harsh explicit override instead of a setting everyone materializes: **`dailyClaudiniteUpdatesRequirePrReview: true`**. Absent means update normally.
4. **`taskScheduler.endpoints` → `taskScheduler.agenticTaskInvocationEndpoints`.** "endpoints" says nothing about which of a dozen possible endpoints these are.
5. **The `claudinite` block dissolves.** `packVersions` moved to the entries (2); `updated` and `ref` are deleted outright; `engineVersion` bubbles to the top level. Everything in that file is Claudinite's — a block named `claudinite` inside it partitioned nothing.

## Why `updated`/`ref` go, and what replaces their four readers

Both hold the provenance of the last **full re-vendor**, not of the current mount — a member converging nightly carries a months-old `ref` and `updated` forever. Our own RULES already say to judge freshness by `engineVersion`/`packVersions` and never by these two (#1065, #786). Deleting them makes that the only thing anyone *can* read.

| Reader | Today | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `vendoring/apply-vendor-set.mjs` anti-rewind guard (#328) | stamped `ref` must be an ancestor of the canon checkout's HEAD | refuse when the target's stamped engine or pack version is **above** this checkout's — the rewind, named directly |
| `update` task precondition | `stamp.ageDays` from `updated` | the mount's own movement in the signal window (`.claudinite/shared/**` touched), which is where every other precondition already gets newness |
| sheepdog `classifyFreshness` | `no-stamp`/`ref-not-on-trunk` from `ref` + a compare call per member | versions only; the `ref-not-on-trunk` states and their per-member canon compare read go away |
| dashboard `activity.mjs` `converged` tile | counts members whose `updated` falls in the window | dropped, and named as absent in the panel's own note — it was a stamp-derived window count, the exact shape #1008 forbids |

## Sequencing

The **filename rename is the migration boundary**, which is what makes this a single pass rather than a stack: a member's currently-vendored engine keeps reading `.claudinite-checks.json` and is unaffected; the new engine reads `.claudinite-settings.json` and falls back to the old name. The migration record rewrites the file into the new shape under the new name; its `appliesTo` probes the member's own mount for the new engine and stays inert until the converge that delivers it has landed.

- [ ] Phase 1 — engine reads and writes the new shape under the new name, legacy name and legacy blocks tolerated on read
- [ ] Phase 2 — migration record: rename + reshape every member's file
- [ ] Phase 3 — cleanup task, a few days later: delete the legacy-name reader and the legacy-block tolerances, gated on no member still carrying the old file

Phase 3's gate is the converge-cycle-confirmable precondition, never a date.

content.content:
# Engine releases

The engine ships as a **version**, not a stream of commits: `ENGINE_VERSION` in
[`version.mjs`](version.mjs) is what a member's stamp records, what an engine
migration's range is written against, and what a pack's `minEngineVersion` is
checked against (`docs/versioned-updates/DESIGN.md` §2). This file is the log of
those versions and the evidence behind each.

The version is date-anchored `<day>.<n>` — `60820.1` for the first release cut on
2026-08-20. [`version.mjs`](version.mjs) states the shape and computes the next
one (`nextVersion`); rows 1 to 6 below predate the format and are the plain
counter it replaced.

## What a release is

**A release is the commit that bumps `ENGINE_VERSION`, and a bump is only
legitimate once the live canary rehearsal has passed against the tree being
released** (owner decision, 2026-08-12). There is no tag and no separate release
artifact: the updater clones `main` at its newest bumped ref, so the version lives
in the file the mount already carries and there is nothing to cut, push or forget.

The canary is what makes the snapshot *qualified*. It converges a real adopting
repo — running **its own** vendored worker, the copy a member would run — against
the ref under test, and asks whether that repo still works. The fixture rehearsal
on every PR only tests what someone remembered to model; this is the other half.

## Releasing

1. Have the change ready on its branch, CI green.
2. Dispatch **Canary rehearsal** with `ref` = your branch
   (`.github/workflows/canary-rehearsal.yml` → Run workflow), and wait for it.
   A red canary is not a release — fix the branch and rehearse again.
3. In the same change: set `ENGINE_VERSION` to `nextVersion` of the one standing
   — a new day restarts the running number at 1 — and add a row below for the new
   version linking the run that passed.
4. Merge. The version now on `main` is the release.

`engine-release-record` (the canon's own local pack) refuses a bump that arrives
without its row, or with a row citing no run — the canary runs in another
repository, so its run id is the only durable evidence the release was rehearsed,

input.body:
Closes #1252

## The end state

```jsonc
{
  "engineVersion": "60823.1",
  "dailyClaudiniteUpdatesRequirePrReview": true,   // optional; absent = update PRs auto-merge
  "packs": [
    { "id": "basics", "version": "60823.1" },
    { "id": "claudinite-growth", "version": "60823.1", "config": { … } }
  ],
  "rules": { … },
  "accept": [ … ],
  "taskScheduler": { "agenticTaskInvocationEndpoints": { … }, "dailyHour": 5, … }
}
```

## What changed, and why each

**The name.** `.claudinite-checks.json` has not been a file of checks since it started carrying the pack declaration, the scheduler anchor, the installed versions and the delivery preference.

**Versions onto their own entries.** The central `claudinite.packVersions` map was keyed by a pack id nothing else in the file had to agree with, so a rename left a version pricing a pack the declaration no longer named (#1041). A version now sits on the entry of the pack it prices, where it cannot be orphaned. One consequence worth naming: a pack pulled in through another's `requires` now gets an entry too, carrying `via` — the corpus's existing marker for "installed, not chosen" — because a version needs somewhere to live. `--init` already seeded exactly that shape.

**`maintenance` goes.** `mechanism` recorded a rollout that finished: its only rival was deleted in #768 Phase 5, so the question had one possible answer for every member that could still ask it. `delivery` was real but materialized into every declaration to state what every member already wanted, so the line said nothing. It becomes a harsh override — `dailyClaudiniteUpdatesRequirePrReview: true` leaves the update PR for a human; absence lands it. `engine/served-by.mjs` is deprecated, not deleted (fielded vendored workers still import it).

**`endpoints` → `agenticTaskInvocationEndpoints`.** "endpoints" said nothing about which of several kinds a scheduler could mean.

**The `claudinite` block dissolves.** `engineVersion` bubbles to the top level; `updated` and `ref` are deleted outright. Both held the provenance of the last **full re-vendor** rather than of the current mount, so a member converging nightly carried a months-old pair forever — our own RULES already said never to judge freshness by them (#1065, #786). Deleting them makes the versions the only thing anyone *can* read. Their four readers:

| Reader | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `apply-vendor-set.mjs` anti-rewind guard (#328) | stamped `ref` must be an ancestor of the canon checkout's HEAD | refuse when anything the target holds is **above** what this checkout would give it — no git history involved, so it now holds on a rootless canon tree too |
| `update` precondition | `stamp.ageDays` from `updated` | whether the mount moved in the signal window, which is where every other precondition gets newness |
| sheepdog `classifyFreshness` | `no-stamp`/`ref-not-on-trunk` + a canon compare per member | versions only; `ref-not-on-trunk` reported a wedge the guard can no longer create, and its per-member read goes with it |
| dashboard `converged` tile | counted members whose `updated` fell in the window | dropped, and named as absent in the panel's own note — a stamp-derived window count is the shape #1008 forbids |

## Sequencing

The filename rename **is** the migration boundary, which is what lets this land in one pass rather than a stack: every reader in the corpus tries both names in `SETTINGS_FILES` order, so a member is read correctly whether or not the record has reached it. `engine/migrations/2026-08-23-settings-file-rename` renames and reshapes each member's file on its own converge (verified idempotent, and against a realistic pre-rename member including a version stamped under a renamed pack's old id). Phase 3 deletes the tolerance, gated on no member still carrying the old name — never on a date.

A rehearsal fixture (`legacy-settings-name`) deliberately carries the retired name, and `rehearsal.test.mjs` fails if no fixture does: with none, the two-name tolerance the whole fleet depends on for that window would be untested.

## Folders this change touches

```
engine/                  two new modules — settings-file.mjs (the two names and the read order)
                         and installed-versions.mjs (where a version lives, read and write).
                         loadConfig gains engineVersion/packVersions/dailyClaudiniteUpdatesRequirePrReview
                         and tolerates the retired blocks; the stamp signal reports installed
                         versions and window movement instead of an age; land-pr gains deliveryFor;
                         selftest probes versions rather than a datetime; served-by deprecated.
engine/migrations/       the rename+reshape record and its applySettingsReshape op; every op now
                         writes back to whichever name the member carries; older records read both.
updates/                 engine/pack/install flows read and write versions through the shape
                         module; engine-update re-resolves the settings path after records run
                         (the record renames the file out from under it).
vendoring/               the vendor writer records versions and nothing about when; the anti-rewind
                         guard is a version comparison; rehearsal modes are stated as installed
                         versions, plus the legacy-name fixture.
packs/claudinite-lifecycle/   update runner: name-tolerant settings lookup, delivery from the
                         override, no mechanism gate; precondition takes newness from the window.
packs/claudinite-fleet-sheepdog/  freshness from versions; ref-not-on-trunk and the per-member
                         canon compare removed; declarations read under either name.
packs/claudinite-dashboard/   mountState reads a declaration; converged tile dropped and named
                         absent; a small settings-read helper for the page's three call sites.
.github/workflows/       the canary reads the canon's renamed settings file.
```

## Still open

`engine/RELEASES.md` carries no row for engine version `60823.1` yet — `engine-release-record` blocks on it by design, since the canary rehearsal runs in another repository and its run id is the only durable evidence. Dispatching the canary against this branch next; the row lands in this PR once it passes.

`.claudinite-checks.json` becomes `.claudinite-settings.json`: it has not been
a file of checks since it started carrying the pack declaration, the scheduler
anchor, the installed versions and the delivery preference.

Four shape changes ride with the rename:

- A pack's installed version moves onto that pack's own entry (`version`). The
  central `claudinite.packVersions` map it replaces was keyed by an id nothing
  else in the file had to agree with, so a rename left a version pricing a pack
  the declaration no longer named (#1041).
- The `maintenance` block goes. `mechanism` recorded a rollout that finished —
  its only rival was deleted in #768 Phase 5 — and `delivery` was materialized
  into every declaration to say what every member already wanted. It becomes an
  override: `dailyClaudiniteUpdatesRequirePrReview: true` leaves the update PR
  for a human, and absence lands it.
- `taskScheduler.endpoints` becomes `agenticTaskInvocationEndpoints`, which
  says which endpoints these are.
- The `claudinite` block dissolves: `engineVersion` bubbles to the top level,
  and `updated`/`ref` are deleted. Both held the provenance of the last FULL
  re-vendor rather than of the current mount, so a member converging nightly
  read as months stale (#1065, #786). Their four readers move to the versions:
  the anti-rewind guard compares versions directly and needs no git history,
  the update precondition takes newness from the mount's own movement in the
  signal window, the sheepdog freshness sweep drops `ref-not-on-trunk` and its
  per-member canon compare, and the dashboard's converged tile is dropped and
  named as absent rather than approximated (#1001, #1008).

The rename is the migration boundary, which is what lets this land in one pass:
every reader tries both names, so a member is read correctly whether or not the
record has reached it, and `engine/migrations/2026-08-23-settings-file-rename`
renames and reshapes each member's file on its own converge. Phase 3 deletes
the tolerance, gated on no member still carrying the old name.

- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- writing-claudinite-skills: Authoring or changing a skill in the Claudinite corpus — SKILL.md conventions, where a skill's checks and tests live, catalog and pack wiring. Use when creating or editing a pack's skills/<name>/ in the canon; a consumer project's own agent docs are authoring-agent-docs' turf.

import re, subprocess, os

def conflicts(path):
    return re.findall(r"<<<<<<< HEAD\n(.*?)=======\n(.*?)>>>>>>> [^\n]*\n", open(path).read(), re.S)

# --- engine/version.mjs: mine (the higher release)
p='engine/version.mjs'
s=open(p).read()
s=re.sub(r"<<<<<<< HEAD\n.*?=======\n(.*?)>>>>>>> [^\n]*\n", r"\1", s, flags=re.S)
open(p,'w').write(s)

# --- pack.mjs: main's shape, my version number
packs = "barriers basics chrome-extension claude-code-web-users-support claudinite-dashboard claudinite-fleet-sheepdog claudinite-growth claudinite-lifecycle node product-wiki python static-website tidy-repo".split()
for pack in packs:
    p=f'packs/{pack}/pack.mjs'
    if not os.path.exists(p): print('MISSING', p); continue
    s=open(p).read()
    def keep_main(m):
        return m.group(1)          # HEAD = main's manifest shape
    s2=re.sub(r"<<<<<<< HEAD\n(.*?)=======\n(.*?)>>>>>>> [^\n]*\n", keep_main, s, flags=re.S)
    # then re-apply my bump on main's version line
    s2=re.sub(r"(\n  version: ')[0-9.]+(',)", r"\g<1>60823.1\g<2>", s2, count=1)
    open(p,'w').write(s2)

# --- VERSIONS.md: both rows, mine (newer) first
for pack in packs:
    p=f'packs/{pack}/VERSIONS.md'
    if not os.path.exists(p): continue
    s=open(p).read()
    def both(m):
        return m.group(2) + m.group(1)   # mine (60823.1) then main's
    s2=re.sub(r"<<<<<<< HEAD\n(.*?)=======\n(.*?)>>>>>>> [^\n]*\n", both, s, flags=re.S)
    open(p,'w').write(s2)
print('done')
PY

`.claudinite-checks.json` becomes `.claudinite-settings.json`: it has not been
a file of checks since it started carrying the pack declaration, the scheduler
anchor, the installed versions and the delivery preference.

Four shape changes ride with the rename:

- A pack's installed version moves onto that pack's own entry (`version`). The
  central `claudinite.packVersions` map it replaces was keyed by an id nothing
  else in the file had to agree with, so a rename left a version pricing a pack
  the declaration no longer named (#1041).

  into every declaration to say what every member already wanted. It becomes an
  override: `dailyClaudiniteUpdatesRequirePrReview: true` leaves the update PR
  for a human, and absence lands it.
- `taskScheduler.endpoints` becomes `agenticTaskInvocationEndpoints`, which
  says which endpoints these are.
- The `claudinite` block dissolves: `engineVersion` bubbles to the top level,
  and `updated`/`ref` are deleted. Both held the provenance of the last FULL
  re-vendor rather than of the current mount, so a member converging nightly
  read as months stale (#1065, #786). Their four readers move to the versions:
  the anti-rewind guard compares versions directly and needs no git history,
  the update precondition takes newness from the mount's own movement in the
  signal window, the sheepdog freshness sweep drops `ref-not-on-trunk` and its
  per-member canon compare, and the dashboard's converged tile is dropped and
  named as absent rather than approximated (#1001, #1008).

The rename is the migration boundary, which is what lets this land in one pass:
every reader tries both names, so a member is read correctly whether or not the
record has reached it, and `engine/migrations/2026-08-23-settings-file-rename`
renames and reshapes each member's file on its own converge. Phase 3 deletes
the tolerance, gated on no member still carrying the old name.

input.body:
Closes #1252

## The end state

```jsonc
{
  "engineVersion": "60823.1",
  "dailyClaudiniteUpdatesRequirePrReview": true,   // optional; absent = update PRs auto-merge
  "packs": [
    { "id": "basics", "version": "60823.1" },
    { "id": "claudinite-growth", "version": "60823.1", "config": { … } }
  ],
  "rules": { … },
  "accept": [ … ],
  "taskScheduler": { "agenticTaskInvocationEndpoints": { … }, "dailyHour": 5, … }
}
```

## What changed, and why each

**The name.** `.claudinite-checks.json` has not been a file of checks since it started carrying the pack declaration, the scheduler anchor, the installed versions and the delivery preference.

**Versions onto their own entries.** The central `claudinite.packVersions` map was keyed by a pack id nothing else in the file had to agree with, so a rename left a version pricing a pack the declaration no longer named (#1041). A version now sits on the entry of the pack it prices, where it cannot be orphaned. One consequence worth naming: a pack pulled in through another's `requires` now gets an entry too, carrying `via` — the corpus's existing marker for "installed, not chosen" — because a version needs somewhere to live. `--init` already seeded exactly that shape.

**`maintenance` goes.** `mechanism` recorded a rollout that finished: its only rival was deleted in #768 Phase 5, so the question had one possible answer for every member that could still ask it. `delivery` was real but materialized into every declaration to state what every member already wanted, so the line said nothing. It becomes a harsh override — `dailyClaudiniteUpdatesRequirePrReview: true` leaves the update PR for a human; absence lands it. `engine/served-by.mjs` is deprecated, not deleted (fielded vendored workers still import it).

**`endpoints` → `agenticTaskInvocationEndpoints`.** "endpoints" said nothing about which of several kinds a scheduler could mean.

**The `claudinite` block dissolves.** `engineVersion` bubbles to the top level; `updated` and `ref` are deleted outright. Both held the provenance of the last **full re-vendor** rather than of the current mount, so a member converging nightly carried a months-old pair forever — our own RULES already said never to judge freshness by them (#1065, #786). Deleting them makes the versions the only thing anyone *can* read. Their four readers:

| Reader | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `apply-vendor-set.mjs` anti-rewind guard (#328) | stamped `ref` must be an ancestor of the canon checkout's HEAD | refuse when anything the target holds is **above** what this checkout would give it — no git history involved, so it now holds on a rootless canon tree too |
| `update` precondition | `stamp.ageDays` from `updated` | whether the mount moved in the signal window, which is where every other precondition gets newness |
| sheepdog `classifyFreshness` | `no-stamp`/`ref-not-on-trunk` + a canon compare per member | versions only; `ref-not-on-trunk` reported a wedge the guard can no longer create, and its per-member read goes with it |
| dashboard `converged` tile | counted members whose `updated` fell in the window | dropped, and named as absent in the panel's own note — a stamp-derived window count is the shape #1008 forbids |

## Sequencing

The filename rename **is** the migration boundary, which is what lets this land in one pass rather than a stack: every reader in the corpus tries both names in `SETTINGS_FILES` order, so a member is read correctly whether or not the record has reached it. `engine/migrations/2026-08-23-settings-file-rename` renames and reshapes each member's file on its own converge (verified idempotent, and against a realistic pre-rename member including a version stamped under a renamed pack's old id). Phase 3 deletes the tolerance, gated on no member still carrying the old name — never on a date.

A rehearsal fixture (`legacy-settings-name`) deliberately carries the retired name, and `rehearsal.test.mjs` fails if no fixture does: with none, the two-name tolerance the whole fleet depends on for that window would be untested.

## Folders this change touches

```
engine/                  two new modules — settings-file.mjs (the two names and the read order)
                         and installed-versions.mjs (where a version lives, read and write).
                         loadConfig gains engineVersion/packVersions/dailyClaudiniteUpdatesRequirePrReview
                         and tolerates the retired blocks; the stamp signal reports installed
                         versions and window movement instead of an age; land-pr gains deliveryFor;
                         selftest probes versions rather than a datetime; served-by deprecated.
engine/migrations/       the rename+reshape record and its applySettingsReshape op; every op now
                         writes back to whichever name the member carries; older records read both.
updates/                 engine/pack/install flows read and write versions through the shape
                         module; engine-update re-resolves the settings path after records run
                         (the record renames the file out from under it).
vendoring/               the vendor writer records versions and nothing about when; the anti-rewind
                         guard is a version comparison; rehearsal modes are stated as installed
                         versions, plus the legacy-name fixture.
packs/claudinite-lifecycle/   update runner: name-tolerant settings lookup, delivery from the
                         override, no mechanism gate; precondition takes newness from the window.
packs/claudinite-fleet-sheepdog/  freshness from versions; ref-not-on-trunk and the per-member
                         canon compare removed; declarations read under either name.
packs/claudinite-dashboard/   mountState reads a declaration; converged tile dropped and named
                         absent; a small settings-read helper for the page's three call sites.
.github/workflows/       the canary reads the canon's renamed settings file.
```

## Release

Engine `60823.1`, rehearsed against this branch's exact head: [run 32609288065](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/32609288065), rebased onto `60822.1` (#1248) first. What that run qualifies specifically is the rename — the canary held a declaration spelled the old way when it began, and the converged tree passed its self-test anyway, which is the shape every member is in for the window between this landing and its own converge.

input.title: Delete the two-name settings-file tolerance once no member carries .claudinite-checks.json
input.body:
Phase 3 of #1252. The rename landed with every reader in the corpus accepting **both** settings-file names, because a member renames its own file only on the converge that carries `engine/migrations/2026-08-23-settings-file-rename`. This issue is the removal of that tolerance.

## The precondition — a converge-cycle fact, never a date

Do not open this on a calendar. The condition is: **no member still carries `.claudinite-checks.json`**, confirmed by reading the fleet's own artifacts rather than assumed from elapsed time. Retiring a tolerance while a member is still on the old shape does not just leave that member behind — every reader then finds no settings file at all, which reads as "declares no packs, never adopted", silently, with green runs to show for it (the same class as #1106).

The sheepdog roster walk already reads each member's declaration under both names, so the cheapest confirmation is to have it report which name each member answered on.

## What comes out

- `engine/settings-file.mjs`: `LEGACY_SETTINGS_FILE`, and `SETTINGS_FILES` collapses to the one name. Everything downstream that maps over it becomes a single path.
- `engine/checks/helpers/repo-context.mjs`: `LEGACY_CONFIG_KEYS` (`claudinite`, `maintenance`) and the two fold-in branches that read them — the legacy `packVersions` map, `claudinite.engineVersion`, and `maintenance.delivery` → `dailyClaudiniteUpdatesRequirePrReview`. A member still declaring either then gets the unknown-setting error, which is correct once none does.
- `engine/installed-versions.mjs`: `LEGACY_STAMP_KEY` and its read path.
- `engine/checks/helpers/repo-context.mjs`: `LEGACY_ENDPOINTS_KEY`, and `SCHEDULE_KEYS` drops `endpoints`.
- `engine/scheduler/land-pr.mjs`: `resolveDelivery`, `deliveryFromChecks`, and `deliveryFor`'s `maintenance.delivery` fallback — gated separately on no fielded vendored worker still importing them (walk the trunk's pack history, per the `updates/*` rule).
- `engine/served-by.mjs`: same gate, same walk. Nothing in canon calls it now.
- The both-name reads in `fleet-api.mjs`, `fleet-reads.mjs`, `signals/fleet.mjs`, `packs/claudinite-dashboard/settings-read.mjs`, `seeds-agree.mjs`, `adopt-pack/checks.mjs`, `selftest.mjs`, and the older migration records that read the declaration.
- The `legacy-settings-name` rehearsal fixture, and the assertion in `rehearsal.test.mjs` that requires exactly one fixture to carry the retired name.
- The retired name in the two `except` lists (`packs/claudinite-lifecycle/declared-checks.json`, `packs/product-wiki/declared-checks.json`), the dashboard stub's `paths:`/`hashFiles`, and the `find` in `environment-setup-command.sh`.

The last three are the ones to check by hand rather than by grep: a stub is copied into a member once and never re-copied, and the setup script is pasted into a container by hand, so both outlive a member's converge by an unknown margin. They come out last, or not at all.

{"id":5224524311,"number":1252,"state":"open","locked":false,"title":"Restructure the member declaration: .claudinite-settings.json, versions on pack entries, dissolve the maintenance and claudinite blocks","body":"The member declaration has accumulated three blocks that no longer say what they are, and one that answers a question nobody asks any more. Owner decisions, this session:

## The end state

```jsonc
{
  "engineVersion": "60820.1",
  "dailyClaudiniteUpdatesRequirePrReview": true,   // optional; absent = update PRs auto-merge
  "packs": [
    { "id": "basics", "version": "60822.1" },
    { "id": "claudinite-growth", "version": "60820.3", "config": { … } }
  ],
  "rules": { … },
  "accept": [ … ],
  "taskScheduler": { "agenticTaskInvocationEndpoints": { … }, "dailyHour": 5, … }
}
```

1. **The file is `.claudinite-settings.json`.** It has never been a file of checks.
2. **A pack's installed version lives on that pack's own entry** (`version`), not in a central `claudinite.packVersions` map keyed by a spelling that a rename can invalidate.
3. **`maintenance` goes.** `mechanism` is the record of a rollout that finished — `versioned` is the only mechanism a repo can be served by, and `baselining` names something that no longer exists. `delivery` is real but every member says `auto-merge`, so it becomes a harsh explicit override instead of a setting everyone materializes: **`dailyClaudiniteUpdatesRequirePrReview: true`**. Absent means update normally.
4. **`taskScheduler.endpoints` → `taskScheduler.agenticTaskInvocationEndpoints`.** "endpoints" says nothing about which of a dozen possible endpoints these are.
5. **The `claudinite` block dissolves.** `packVersions` moved to the entries (2); `updated` and `ref` are deleted outright; `engineVersion` bubbles to the top level. Everything in that file is Claudinite's — a block named `claudinite` inside it partitioned nothing.

## Why `updated`/`ref` go, and what replaces their four readers

Both hold the provenance of the last **full re-vendor**, not of the current mount — a member converging nightly carries a months-old `ref` and `updated` forever. Our own RULES already say to judge freshness by `engineVersion`/`packVersions` and never by these two (#1065, #786). Deleting them makes that the only thing anyone *can* read.

| Reader | Today | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `vendoring/apply-vendor-set.mjs` anti-rewind guard (#328) | stamped `ref` must be an ancestor of the canon checkout's HEAD | refuse when the target's stamped engine or pack version is **above** this checkout's — the rewind, named directly |
| `update` task precondition | `stamp.ageDays` from `updated` | the mount's own movement in the signal window (`.claudinite/shared/**` touched), which is where every other precondition already gets newness |
| sheepdog `classifyFreshness` | `no-stamp`/`ref-not-on-trunk` from `ref` + a compare call per member | versions only; the `ref-not-on-trunk` states and their per-member canon compare read go away |
| dashboard `activity.mjs` `converged` tile | counts members whose `updated` falls in the window | dropped, and named as absent in the panel's own note — it was a stamp-derived window count, the exact shape #1008 forbids |

## Sequencing

The **filename rename is the migration boundary**, which is what makes this a single pass rather than a stack: a member's currently-vendored engine keeps reading `.claudinite-checks.json` and is unaffected; the new engine reads `.claudinite-settings.json` and falls back to the old name. The migration record rewrites the file into the new shape under the new name; its `appliesTo` probes the member's own mount for the new engine and stays inert until the converge that delivers it has landed.

- [ ] Phase 1 — engine reads and writes the new shape under the new name, legacy name and legacy blocks tolerated on read
- [ ] Phase 2 — migration record: rename + reshape every member's file
- [ ] Phase 3 — cleanup task, a few days later: delete the legacy-name reader and the legacy-block tolerances, gated on no member still carrying the old file

Phase 3's gate is the converge-cycle-confirmable precondition, never a date.

Both hold the provenance of the last **full re-vendor**, not of the current mount — a member converging nightly carries a months-old `ref` and `updated` forever. Our own RULES already say to judge freshness by `engineVersion`/`packVersions` and never by these two (#1065, #786). Deleting them makes that the only thing anyone *can* read.

| Reader | Today | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `vendoring/apply-vendor-set.mjs` anti-rewind guard (#328) | stamped `ref` must be an ancestor of the canon checkout's HEAD | refuse when the target's stamped engine or pack version is **above** this checkout's — the rewind, named directly |
| `update` task precondition | `stamp.ageDays` from `updated` | the mount's own movement in the signal window (`.claudinite/shared/**` touched), which is where every other precondition already gets newness |
| sheepdog `classifyFreshness` | `no-stamp`/`ref-not-on-trunk` from `ref` + a compare call per member | versions only; the `ref-not-on-trunk` states and their per-member canon compare read go away |
| dashboard `activity.mjs` `converged` tile | counts members whose `updated` falls in the window | dropped, and named as absent in the panel's own note — it was a stamp-derived window count, the exact shape #1008 forbids |

## Sequencing

The **filename rename is the migration boundary**, which is what makes this a single pass rather than a stack: a member's currently-vendored engine keeps reading `.claudinite-checks.json` and is unaffected; the new engine reads `.claudinite-settings.json` and falls back to the old name. The migration record rewrites the file into the new shape under the new name; its `appliesTo` probes the member's own mount for the new engine and stays inert until the converge that delivers it has landed.

- [ ] Phase 1 — engine reads and writes the new shape under the new name, legacy name and legacy blocks tolerated on read
- [ ] Phase 2 — migration record: rename + reshape every member's file
- [ ] Phase 3 — cleanup task, a few days later: delete the legacy-name reader and the legacy-block tolerances, gated on no member still carrying the old file

Phase 3's gate is the converge-cycle-confirmable precondition, never a date.

CI is green — tests, both conformance sweeps, and the write-surface gate all passed on the final head.

**Answers to your three questions**

**Why `maintenance` was still there** — it wasn't earning its keep, and both halves are now gone. `mechanism` was the skew guard from the #768 rollout: it kept `baselining` and the versioned flows from converging one mount at once. Phase 5 deleted `baselining`, so the field had exactly one possible answer for every member that could still ask it. `delivery` was real, but the corpus rule "automation materializes the explicit value into every file it maintains" wrote `auto-merge` into every declaration to state what every member already wanted — a line that says nothing. It's now the override you specified: `dailyClaudiniteUpdatesRequirePrReview: true`, absent means land it.

**Why `endpoints` was blandly named** — no better reason than that it was named for what it held rather than what it's for. Renamed to `agenticTaskInvocationEndpoints`; the old spelling stays readable until each member's converge rewrites it.

**The `claudinite` block** — your suspicion was right on all three counts. `packVersions` moved to the entries, `engineVersion` bubbled up, and the block is gone. `updated`/`ref` did have four live readers, but every one of them was reading the wrong thing: both fields record the last *full re-vendor*, not the last converge, so a member converging nightly carried a months-old pair forever. Our own RULES already said never to judge freshness by them (#1065, #786) — deleting them makes the versions the only thing anyone *can* read. The anti-rewind guard is now a direct version comparison (and no longer needs git history at all), the update precondition takes newness from the mount's own movement in the window, the sheepdog sweep loses a per-member API call along with `ref-not-on-trunk`, and the dashboard's converged tile is dropped and named as absent rather than approximated.

Two things worth flagging: the version-on-entry move forced `requires`-closure packs to get entries too (carrying `via`, the existing "installed, not chosen" marker) since a version needs somewhere to live — `--init` already seeded that shape. And I rebased onto #1248 mid-flight and re-ran the canary against the final head, so the release row cites the tree that actually ships.

- [#1259](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1259) — the change, CI green, canary [run 32609288065](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/32609288065)
- [#1252](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1252) — the tracking issue
- [#1264](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1264) — Phase 3, filed as its sub-issue: delete the two-name tolerance, gated on no member still carrying the old file, never on a date

> ⚠️ Still open: #1259 needs your review — it releases engine `60823.1` and renames a file in every member repo. One deliberate leftover: `docs/per-project-scheduling/DESIGN.md` and `MIGRATION.md` still say `.claudinite-checks.json`, left alone because they're dated records of a past migration.

---
name: merge-to-main
description: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
---

# Merge to main

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent
points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.

1. Load `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request` in one `ToolSearch`.
2. No PR open for the branch? `create_pull_request` (base `main`), body ending `Closes #<issue>`.
3. If the PR has check runs, wait for them to pass. None — merge without waiting.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Don't pre-read
   mergeability; the call fails loudly.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.
6. Capture the conversation:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`
   (in the canon repo: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`). Skip only if
   the repo doesn't declare `claudinite-growth`. A later merge in the same session runs it again.
7. Run the basics pack's
   [verify-in-production](../../../basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md) skill, unasked.
   This step is that skill's **only** trigger — it files against what the squash actually landed,
   which is why it runs here and not when the code was written or the PR opened. It decides
   whether this change needs a production check at all — most don't — and files the issue that
   comes back once the change is live. Never offer the owner to check later instead.

Don't re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge.

| 60822.1 | — | `usage-fold` folds daily rather than hourly, and its signal window moves with it — a frequency finer than the cron's two ticks a day cannot be honoured, and a window still sized to an hour would never see a captured session again (§17.1). `growth-extract`'s anchor offset retires; the `schedule_after:` it already declared is what orders it. The ordering field is renamed `after` → `schedule_after`: it names task ids, not a time, and what it steers is when the item is scheduled onto an executor. `after` is normalized at the door forever and draws an advisory rename, so a member's own task file keeps working. |

  Why: a member receives a pack directory only when the canon's version exceeds the one it has installed, so content edited without a bump reaches nobody while canon CI reports it shipped (#939 froze seven repos for five days that way); an unrecorded bump is the same evidence gap on a smaller scale — "what did version N change?" becomes unanswerable once the commit scrolls out of history
  Fix: raise `version` in packs/product-wiki/pack.mjs to '60823.2' — the version is the whole delivery signal, so an edit that does not move it stays in the canon forever
  More: docs/versioned-updates/DESIGN.md

`.claudinite-checks.json` becomes `.claudinite-settings.json`: it has not been
a file of checks since it started carrying the pack declaration, the scheduler
anchor, the installed versions and the delivery preference.

Four shape changes ride with the rename:

- A pack's installed version moves onto that pack's own entry (`version`). The
  central `claudinite.packVersions` map it replaces was keyed by an id nothing
  else in the file had to agree with, so a rename left a version pricing a pack
  the declaration no longer named (#1041).
- The `maintenance` block goes. `mechanism` recorded a rollout that finished —
  its only rival was deleted in #768 Phase 5 — and `delivery` was materialized
  into every declaration to say what every member already wanted. It becomes an
  override: `dailyClaudiniteUpdatesRequirePrReview: true` leaves the update PR
  for a human, and absence lands it.
- `taskScheduler.endpoints` becomes `agenticTaskInvocationEndpoints`, which
  says which endpoints these are.
- The `claudinite` block dissolves: `engineVersion` bubbles to the top level,
  and `updated`/`ref` are deleted. Both held the provenance of the last FULL
  re-vendor rather than of the current mount, so a member converging nightly
  read as months stale (#1065, #786). Their four readers move to the versions:
  the anti-rewind guard compares versions directly and needs no git history,
  the update precondition takes newness from the mount's own movement in the
  signal window, the sheepdog freshness sweep drops `ref-not-on-trunk` and its
  per-member canon compare, and the dashboard's converged tile is dropped and
  named as absent rather than approximated (#1001, #1008).

The rename is the migration boundary, which is what lets this land in one pass:
every reader tries both names, so a member is read correctly whether or not the
record has reached it, and `engine/migrations/2026-08-23-settings-file-rename`
renames and reshapes each member's file on its own converge. Phase 3 deletes
the tolerance, gated on no member still carrying the old name.
